an3.57:1.1: Vacchagotta appears frequently throughout the Suttas as a dedicated questioner of the Buddha, and a gradually converted skeptic. The “Vacchagotta trilogy” ([mn71]()–3) traces his spiritual development. These are supplemented by an entire Saṁyutta of questions ([sn33.1]()).
an3.57:1.3: The same calumny is reported at [mn56:17.4](), [an8.12:27.6](), and [pli-tv-kd6:31.11.4](). In all of those cases, the ill-report is traceable back to the Jains. Vacchagotta was clearly interested in Jain teachings, as he inquires about them in [mn71](). His own actual beliefs are hard to pin down, and it seems likely that before his final conversion to Buddhism he was curious and skeptical about all religions.
